title: AI chat assistant for collection and request workflows powered by Cerebras
summary: Add a chat interface that lets users interact with a Cerebras-powered AI assistant scoped strictly to their collections, requests, and API execution. The assistant can answer questions about saved requests, execute single or batch API calls within a collection, and consolidate results for the user.
userValue: Enables conversational API testing workflows where users can ask the assistant to run all requests in a collection, compare results, or answer questions about their saved requests—without switching context or manually triggering each request.
problemStatement: Users with large collections must manually select and execute requests one-by-one. There is no way to ask questions about request structure, batch-execute a collection, or get a consolidated summary of results without leaving the app and using external tools.
assumptions: Cerebras provides an OpenAI-compatible REST API at https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/chat/completions with Bearer token auth.
The user will supply their own Cerebras API key; the app does not ship or proxy keys.
The first implementation uses the llama3.1-8b model for speed and low token cost; the model can be made configurable later.
The chat assistant is strictly scoped to collections, requests, and API execution—general-purpose or off-topic responses are blocked by the system prompt.
The existing executeRequest function in requestExecution.ts is reused for actual API execution.
The API key is stored in the browser only (localStorage) and never logged, exported, or sent to any endpoint other than Cerebras.
Streaming is desirable but not required for the first slice.

in: Chat icon button visible in the app shell that opens a modal chat interface
API key prompt screen shown on first open or when no valid key is stored
Validate the Cerebras API key with a lightweight test call before accepting it
Conversational chat UI with message history, user input, and assistant responses
System prompt that injects the user's current collections and request metadata (names, methods, URLs) as context
System prompt guardrails that restrict responses to collections, requests, and API execution only
Ability to execute a single request by name or ID when the user asks
Ability to batch-execute all requests in a named collection and consolidate results
Redact secrets, auth tokens, and sensitive header values before sending any context to Cerebras
Display execution results inline in the chat with status, duration, and response summary
Persist chat history per session (cleared on page reload)
out: Server-side API key proxy or backend service
Persisting chat history across sessions or to IndexedDB in the first slice
Streaming token-by-token responses in the first slice
Allowing the AI to modify, create, or delete requests or collections
General-purpose conversation, code generation, or non-app-related queries
Model selection UI in the first slice
Token usage tracking or billing dashboard

acceptanceCriteria: A chat icon button is visible in the app shell and opens a modal overlay.
If no Cerebras API key is stored, the modal shows a key input form with a link to cloud.cerebras.ai.
The entered API key is validated with a test chat completion call; invalid keys show a clear error.
Valid API keys are stored in localStorage under a namespaced key and never logged or exported.
Once authenticated, the user sees a chat interface with a message input and scrollable message history.
The system prompt includes a redacted snapshot of the user's collections and request metadata.
The assistant only responds to queries about the user's collections, requests, and API execution; off-topic prompts receive a polite refusal.
The user can ask the assistant to execute a specific request and see the result inline.
The user can ask the assistant to execute all requests in a collection; results are batched and summarized.
Secrets, auth tokens, and sensitive header values are redacted before being sent to Cerebras in the system prompt.
Execution errors (network failures, 4xx/5xx) are surfaced clearly in the chat without exposing raw secrets.
The chat modal can be closed and reopened without losing session messages.
Closing and reopening the key prompt does not lose a previously stored valid key.
securityConsiderations: The Cerebras API key is stored only in localStorage under a namespaced key and is never included in exports, diagnostics, or AI context.
All request metadata sent to Cerebras as system prompt context must pass through the existing redactRequestForAi pipeline.
Auth config values (tokens, passwords, API keys from request auth fields) are never included in chat context.
Environment variable values marked as secret are excluded from the context snapshot.
The system prompt explicitly instructs the model to never reveal API keys, tokens, or credentials in responses.
Response bodies from executed requests are summarized, not sent raw to the LLM, to avoid leaking sensitive API responses.
The API key input field uses type=password and the key is masked in the UI after entry.
testPlan: Unit tests for the Cerebras API client module: successful completion, error handling, key validation.
Unit tests for the context builder: redaction of secrets, correct metadata shape, collection/request snapshot generation.
Unit tests for the system prompt: verifying guardrail instructions are present and no raw secrets are included.
Unit tests for batch execution: concurrent request execution, result aggregation, error handling per request.
UI tests for the chat modal: open/close, key prompt flow, message send/receive, result display.
Security tests: confirm no secret values appear in outbound Cerebras payloads or in chat message history.
Integration test with a mock Cerebras endpoint: full conversation round-trip with execute intent.

firstImplementationSlice.title: Chat modal with Cerebras API key prompt, basic Q&A about collections/requests, and single-request execution
firstImplementationSlice.goal: Let a user open a chat modal, enter their Cerebras API key, ask questions about their saved collections and requests, and execute a single request by name with the result shown inline.
scope: Add a chat FAB icon to the app shell (replacing or alongside the existing Help FAB).
Create a ChatModal component with three states: key-prompt, chat, and loading.
Build a CerebrasClient module in src/lib/ai/cerebrasClient.ts that calls the REST API directly with fetch.
Build a ChatContextBuilder in src/lib/ai/chatContext.ts that produces a redacted snapshot of all collections and their requests for the system prompt.
Build a system prompt template that includes the context snapshot and guardrail instructions.
Wire the chat input to send messages to Cerebras and display responses.
Parse assistant responses for execution intents (e.g. 'I will now execute request X') and trigger executeRequest.
Display execution results (status, duration, body preview) as a structured chat message.
outOfScope: Batch execution of all requests in a collection (second slice).
Model selection or advanced Cerebras parameters.
Allowing the assistant to modify request or collection data.
acceptanceCriteria: A chat icon button is visible and opens the ChatModal.
The modal prompts for a Cerebras API key if none is stored.
The key is validated with a test call and stored in localStorage on success.
The user can type a message and receive a response from Cerebras.
The assistant can answer questions about collections and request names, methods, and URLs.
Off-topic questions receive a polite refusal message.
The user can ask the assistant to execute a named request and see status, duration, and body preview in the chat.
No secret values appear in the outbound Cerebras API payload.
testPlan: Unit tests for CerebrasClient: successful chat completion, API error handling, key validation call.
Unit tests for ChatContextBuilder: redacted snapshot shape, secret exclusion, empty-collection handling.
UI test for ChatModal: open modal, enter key, send message, verify response appears.

secondImplementationSlice.title: Batch collection execution and consolidated result summaries
secondImplementationSlice.goal: Allow the user to ask the assistant to execute all requests in a collection, run them concurrently, and present a consolidated summary with per-request status, timing, and error details.
scope: Detect batch execution intent in assistant responses (e.g. 'execute all requests in Collection X').
Execute all requests in the target collection using the existing executeRequest function with Promise.allSettled.
Build a BatchResultSummary component that shows a table of request name, method, URL, status, duration, and body preview.
Send the consolidated summary back to the assistant for natural language analysis.
Handle partial failures gracefully: show which requests succeeded and which failed.
acceptanceCriteria: The user can ask 'run all requests in [collection name]' and the assistant executes them.
Results are displayed in a structured table within the chat.
The assistant provides a natural language summary of the batch results.
Individual request failures do not block other requests from executing.
The consolidated summary does not include raw secret values from responses.

documentationUpdates: Add AI Chat feature description to README feature list.
Add in-app help content describing the chat assistant's capabilities and limitations.
Document the Cerebras API key setup steps and link to cloud.cerebras.ai.
Update acceptance criteria docs when each slice is implemented.
notes: Planned on 2026-05-04: feature spec created based on user request for a chat interface powered by Cerebras.
The Cerebras API is OpenAI-compatible, so the client module can potentially be reused for other providers later.
The system prompt must be carefully crafted to prevent prompt injection and off-topic responses.
llama3.1-8b is chosen for the first slice due to speed; gpt-oss-120b is available for complex reasoning if needed.
Batch execution uses Promise.allSettled to ensure partial failures don't block the full run.
Chat history is session-only in the first slice to avoid storing potentially sensitive conversation data in IndexedDB.
